industrie.title: Cool roofs for industrial buildings and workshops | ALBEDIA
industrie.desc: Reflective roofs for workshops and production sites: less heat coming through the roof and more bearable workstations in summer.
industrie.lead: Workshops and production sites combine the heat of the machines with the heat of the roof. A reflective roof reduces the second, over the whole surface of the building.
industrie.enjeux_titre: When the roof adds to the heat of the process
enjeux: In a workshop, the roof is often the largest surface exposed to the sun. Dark and poorly insulated, it adds its heat gains to the heat given off by machines, furnaces and compressors. During heatwaves, working conditions deteriorate quickly.

Reducing the heat that comes in through the roof helps keep temperatures more bearable for operators, eases the load on ventilation or cooling systems and protects temperature-sensitive processes and stock.
batiments: Storage halls for materials and finished products
benefices: Less heat radiated by the roof above the workstations.
If the site is air-conditioned or ventilated, the equipment works less during heat peaks.
Smaller temperature swings for the roof covering and waterproofing, day after day.
points: The type and condition of the roof: metal deck, bituminous or synthetic waterproofing, fibre cement
Smoke vents, rooflights, ducts and equipment to protect during the works
Site constraints: access, prevention plan, hazardous areas and working hours
The fire performance required for the roof, especially on classified industrial sites
industrie.aides: In France, CEE sheet BAT-EN-112 targets tertiary buildings in commercial use. For an industrial site, we review case by case the incentive schemes that may apply, in France or in the other countries where we work.

logistique.title: Cool roofs for warehouses and logistics hubs | ALBEDIA
logistique.desc: Reflective roofs for warehouses and logistics hubs: limit the heat that builds up under the roof, for staff and for goods.
logistique.h1: Cool roofs for warehouses and logistics hubs
logistique.lead: Warehouses have huge roofs that are often poorly insulated. Making them reflective limits the heat that builds up under the roof covering.
logistique.enjeux_titre: Thousands of square metres in full sun
enjeux: A single-storey warehouse often means several thousand square metres of roof exposed to the sun, above a volume that is rarely air-conditioned. In summer, heat builds up under the roof and spreads to the picking and storage areas.
For order pickers, forklift drivers and goods, every degree counts. A cool roof acts at the source, over the whole roof, without changing how the building is operated.
benefices: Less heat radiated towards the aisles, loading docks and picking stations.
Less heat building up in storage areas during heatwaves.
Offices, temperature-controlled areas and plant rooms need less energy.
points: The area and condition of the roof, often metal deck or bituminous waterproofing
Rooflights and smoke vents to preserve
Any solar panels and their walkways
Roof access and the safety of the people working on it
logistique.aides: In France, warehouses fall under the tertiary decree from 1,000 m² of tertiary activity, and reducing the cooling needs of air-conditioned areas can help meet its targets. CEE sheet BAT-EN-112 targets tertiary buildings in commercial use: we check your eligibility. Rules differ in Switzerland, Italy and Spain: we review your case during the study.

distribution.title: Cool roofs for shops and retail stores | ALBEDIA
distribution.desc: Reflective roofs for air-conditioned shops and sales floors: less heat to remove, air conditioning under less strain, possible incentives.
distribution.h1: Cool roofs for shops and sales floors
distribution.lead: Shops and supermarkets are almost always air-conditioned: every unit of heat that does not come in through the roof is one the air conditioning does not have to remove.
distribution.enjeux_titre: Air conditioning working against the sun
enjeux: A sales floor combines a large roof, lighting, refrigeration equipment and many visitors. In summer, the air conditioning runs at full power to keep customers and staff comfortable.
By limiting the solar gains through the roof, a cool roof reduces the cooling load. In France, this is exactly the case covered by the CEE scheme BAT-EN-112, which can fund part of the works.
benefices: Less heat to remove and lower power peaks during heatwaves.
For customers and staff alike, especially under poorly insulated roofs.
In France, under conditions, the CEE bonus BAT-EN-112 can cover part of the investment.
points: The heating and cooling system: in France, sheet BAT-EN-112 requires a heat pump system
Rooftop equipment: chillers, air handling units, ducts
Organising the works outside opening hours if necessary
The fire performance of the roof for buildings open to the public
distribution.aides: In France, CEE sheet BAT-EN-112 can apply if your shop is a tertiary building in commercial use, with the roof above an air-conditioned volume and heating and cooling by heat pump. Premises of 1,000 m² and more are also subject to the tertiary decree. In the other countries, we review the incentives available for your project.

tertiaire.title: Cool roofs for offices and service buildings | ALBEDIA
tertiaire.desc: Reflective roofs for offices and service buildings: reduce cooling needs and lower the energy consumption of the building.
tertiaire.h1: Cool roofs for offices and service buildings
tertiaire.lead: For an air-conditioned office building, the roof is a simple lever to reduce cooling needs, alongside the other energy-saving actions.
tertiaire.enjeux_titre: Top floors on the front line
enjeux: Top floors and single-storey buildings take the heat of the roof directly. In air-conditioned offices, this means high summer consumption. In offices without air conditioning, it means discomfort that weighs on work.

A cool roof is a quick action to carry out, with no work inside the building. Its value depends on the share of air conditioning in the building's consumption: we assess it before proposing it to you.
batiments: Air-conditioned open-plan offices and call centres
benefices: Fewer solar gains through the roof, so less cooling to produce.
The floors under the roof are the first to benefit from a cooler roof.
A consumption-reduction measure to document in your energy action plan.
points: The share of heating and cooling in the consumption
The insulation level of the roof
Technical equipment installed on the roof terrace
Co-ownership or lease rules for work on the roof
tertiaire.aides: In France, the tertiary decree requires buildings of 1,000 m² and more to cut their final energy consumption by 40% in 2030, 50% in 2040 and 60% in 2050, and the CEE bonus BAT-EN-112 can apply to tertiary buildings in commercial use: we check your case. In the other countries, we check what applies to your building.

collectivites.title: Cool roofs for schools, sports halls and public buildings | ALBEDIA
collectivites.desc: Reflective roofs for public buildings: schools, sports halls and municipal workshops that stay usable during heatwaves.
collectivites.lead: Schools, sports halls, municipal workshops: buildings that must remain usable during periods of intense heat.
collectivites.enjeux_titre: Keeping public facilities usable in summer
enjeux: Heatwaves put public buildings to the test, as they often have little or no air conditioning. Under a dark roof, classrooms, sports halls and reception areas become hard to use.
A cool roof is a simple adaptation measure that can be applied to existing roofs. At neighbourhood scale, lighter roofs also help limit urban heat islands.
benefices: Buildings that stay usable in summer
Less heat under the roofs of classrooms, sports halls and reception areas.
A visible action against extreme heat, applied to your existing buildings.
For air-conditioned rooms, less cooling to produce.
points: The fire performance requirements for the roof of buildings open to the public
The timing of the works, for example during school holidays
The condition and type of the roofs across your buildings
An asbestos survey for older buildings, before any work
collectivites.aides: In France, public buildings housing 1,000 m² or more of tertiary activities are subject to the tertiary decree. Wherever your buildings are, we help you document the value of a cool roof in your action plan.

agricole.title: Cool roofs for agricultural buildings | ALBEDIA
agricole.desc: Reflective roofs for livestock, storage and processing buildings: less heat under the roof for animals, crops and people.
agricole.lead: Livestock, storage and processing buildings: limiting the heat that comes in through the roof protects the animals, the crops and the people who work there.
enjeux: Agricultural buildings often have large lightweight roofs, in metal deck or fibre cement, with no insulation. In summer, heat builds up quickly.
A reflective roof reduces solar gains without changing the structure of the building. Its value is assessed case by case, depending on how the building is used and ventilated.
benefices: More bearable temperatures for animals and people.
Less heat in storage and processing areas.
The coating is applied to the existing roof covering.
points: Fibre cement sheets: an asbestos survey is essential before any work
The ventilation of the building, which determines the gain
The strength of the roof covering and safe access
Translucent rooflight sheets to preserve
agricole.aides: Incentives vary with the activity, the status of the farm and the country. We review them with you during the study.
